text.p: Video game company 3DO Co., in a major switch in strategy, announced a corporate restructuring to focus entirely on the Internet and game software and will sell its hardware business or convert it into a joint venture.

As part of the reorganization, President Hugh Martin will assume full operating control of 3DO, the video game equipment and software company said in a statement. Its highly visible chairman and chief executive, Trip Hawkins, will remain in those posts but will shift his focus to the role of creative director.

"The Internet, and Internet entertainment in particular, is a huge opportunity," Hawkins said in the statement. "We are moving toward focusing entirely on the challenge of building a strong entertainment software studio, with the Internet as a catalyst for growth."

3DO plans to launch its first Internet product Tuesday, Merdian 59, a multiplayer game set in a fantasy world. It pointed out that 25,000 people had signed up to play the game in an early free trial even though little money was spent on advertising.
The company said it expected the sale of its 3DO Systems hardware business or a joint venture would cut the number of jobs from 450 to 300.
3DO stock dropped $1.25 to $6.875 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.

The Redwood City, Calif., company was founded in 1991 as a maker of advanced video game systems. It drew media attention because its founder, Hawkins, founded a successful entertainment software company, Electronic Arts, and because its 32-bit video game system was ahead of the 16-bit systems of the time, with sharper, more realistic graphics.

But, with a video game system whose initial $700 price was much higher than rival systems and against stiff competition from the likes of Nintendo Co. Ltd. and Sega Enterprises Ltd., its business never took off. The company now makes 64-bit games as well as 32-bit systems.
3DO, which went public in 1993, did not report its first profit until last May, when it posted net income of $1.2 million on revenues of $14.7 million in its fourth fiscal quarter.

As part of the reorganization, 3DO said it has taken steps to cut spending by eliminating entertainment projects with outside developers and reassigning company employees to its most promising software titles.

"The game business climate right now dictates that we make hits and conserve cash," said Martin. "Now we can concentrate on our most compelling entertainment software products while spending less capital, making better products and getting into position for Internet-driven growth."
Hawkins said, "Hardware and software are very different businesses, and 3DO needs to simplify and focus its efforts.
"Our potential hardware technology customers would like broader access to 3DO's proprietary technologies and a closer partnership, and that argues for a potential joint venture," he said.
3DO recently licensed its 64-bit technology to Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. Ltd. for $100 million.

On Monday, it stressed that it remained committed to supporting the Japanese company's efforts to launch products based on the technology and that it did not expect its reorganization strategy to affect that project.
